Finite verb with its phrasal particle; rule 44 keeps the head on the verb, since forth names nothing. The unit is discontinuous, English holding the verb back to the end of the subject (rule 25).

Rectum with of (rule 19) and its indefinite article (rule 15); discontinuous around the gentilic adjective (rule 25).

The ASV recasts the waw's clause as a relative and writes no separate connective; rule 17 gives the relative to the explicit pronoun, not to the waw.

The generic head noun אִישׁ with the gentilic naming the class is rendered by one English word, so the two share a unit under rule 30, headed on the lexeme-bearing gentilic; the indefinite article joins it (rule 15) and the verbless clause's copula joins the predicate (rule 20).
בְּתוֹךְ rendered by the single word among fuses under rule 30, headed on the lexeme-bearing noun.

review_notes: The clause וְהוּא בֶּן־אִישׁ מִצְרִי is recast as whose father was an Egyptian: rule 17 puts the relative on the explicit pronoun and leaves the waw unrepresented, and rule 30's generic-head-noun clause fuses אִישׁ מִצְרִי into the one word Egyptian.
